labels:
- region "F1·01 Configurable number line":
  - heading "F1·01 Configurable number line" [level=2]
  - group: "Spec card ★ GCSE: Extension: thousands with step 250, hundredths 2.3–2.4 for bounds and rounding"
  - paragraph:
    - strong: "Year groups:"
    - text: KS3 Years 7–9 (12–15).
    - strong: "Linked components:"
    - text: F0-02, F0-04, F0-05, F0-11, F0-12, F1-02, F1-03.
  - heading "Live demo · F1-01" [level=3]
  - tablist "Configurable number line modes":
    - tab "Watch" [selected]
    - tab "Guided"
    - tab "Explore"
    - tab "Challenge"
  - button "Restore defaults"
  - text: Number line · Big numbers step 7/7
  - img "Number line 0 to 10000.": 0 2000 4000 6000 8000 10000 6750
  - text: between
  - math "6000 and 8000": 6000 a n d 8000
  - text: nearer
  - math "6000"
  - text: Big numbers
  - img "Big numbers (Nova the cat, welcome)":
    - img "Nova the cat, goodbye"
  - img "Sir Bob Maximus, pleased"
  - text: Sir Bob Maximus · watch The same line works for thousands. Each line is two thousand, so this point is six thousand seven hundred and fifty.
  - img "Nova the cat, cheering"
  - status: "Nova: Flawless. Like me."
  - group "Animation controls":
    - button "Reset"
    - button "Step back"
    - button "Play"
    - button "Step forward" [disabled]
    - text: Step 7 of 7 · Big numbers
    - slider "Scrub through steps": "6"

  - text: value
  - math "0.125"

    - img "Nova the cat, goodbye"
  - img "Sir Bob Maximus, pleased"

- region "F1·03 Jump-arc operator":
  - heading "F1·03 Jump-arc operator" [level=2]
  - group: "Spec card ★ GCSE: Extension: directed numbers to −30 and decimal jumps"
  - paragraph:

  - img "Sir Bob Maximus, pleased"

- region "F1·05 Rounding rolling-ball":
  - heading "F1·05 Rounding rolling-ball" [level=2]
  - group: "Spec card ★ GCSE: Extension: 2 dp and negative numbers"
  - paragraph:
    - strong: "Year groups:"
    - text: KS3 Years 7–9 (12–15).
    - strong: "Linked components:"
    - text: F1-01, F1-02, F1-08, F1-11, F0-04, F0-12.
  - heading "Live demo · F1-05" [level=3]

    - tab "Watch" [selected]
    - tab "Guided"
    - tab "Explore"
    - tab "Challenge"
  - button "Restore defaults"
  - text: Rounding · Negatives step 7/7
  - 'img "Rounding −23 to the nearest 10: between −30 and −20, rounds to −20."': −30 −29 −28 −27 −26 −25 −24 −23 −22 −21 −20 half way −25 −23
  - text: −23
  - math "≈ −20"
  - text: Negatives
  - img "Negatives (Nova the cat, welcome)":
    - img "Nova the cat, goodbye"
  - img "Sir Bob Maximus, pleased"
  - text: Sir Bob Maximus · watch Negatives work the same way. Minus 23 is between minus 30 and minus 20, nearer minus 20, so it rounds to minus 20.
  - img "Nova the cat, cheering"
  - status: "Nova: Flawless. Like me."
  - group "Animation controls":
    - button "Reset"
    - button "Step back"
    - button "Play"
    - button "Step forward" [disabled]
    - text: Step 7 of 7 · Negatives
    - slider "Scrub through steps": "6"

  - text: end
  - math "filled equals included": f i l l e d = i n c l u d e d
  - text: x ≥ 1.5

    - img "Nova the cat, goodbye"
  - img "Sir Bob Maximus, pleased"
  - text: Sir Bob Maximus · watch Solutions are not only whole numbers. x is at least 1.5, so 1.5, 1.8 and 2.75 all work.

- region "F1·08 Estimation line":
  - heading "F1·08 Estimation line" [level=2]
  - group: "Spec card ★ GCSE: Extension: 1 s.f. estimates with small decimals, square-root bounds"
  - paragraph:
    - strong: "Year groups:"
    - text: KS3 Years 7–9 (12–15).

  - button "Restore defaults"

  - img "Estimate of √50 on a number line.": 6 7 8 9 √49 = 7 √64 = 8 = 7.071
  - text: √50
  - math "between 7 and 8": b e t w e e n 7 a n d 8
  - text: ≈
  - math "7.071"
  - text: Square roots
  - img "Square roots (Nova the cat, welcome)":
    - img "Nova the cat, goodbye"
  - img "Sir Bob Maximus, look here"
  - text: "Sir Bob Maximus · watch Square root of 50 is not a whole number. 49 is 7 squared and 64 is 8 squared, so root 50 is just over 7. It is irrational: the decimal never ends."
  - img "Nova the cat, pointing"
  - status: "Nova: Flawless. Like me."

options.label: GCSE: square of side 5 cm (perimeter bounds)

labels:
- region "F1·11 Error-interval line":
  - heading "F1·11 Error-interval line" [level=2]
  - group: "Spec card ★ GCSE: Extension: bounds in calculations (perimeter, and later area and speed)"
  - paragraph:
    - strong: "Year groups:"
    - text: KS3 Years 7–9 (12–15).
    - strong: "Linked components:"
    - text: F1-05, F1-06, F1-08, F1-09, F0-04.
  - heading "Live demo · F1-11" [level=3]
  - tablist "Error-interval line modes":
    - tab "Watch" [selected]
    - tab "Guided"
    - tab "Explore"
    - tab "Challenge"
  - button "Restore defaults"
  - text: Error interval · Bounds in a calculation step 6/6
  - img "Error interval 4.5 ≤ x < 5.5.": 4 4.5 5 5.5 6 measured 5 cm 4.5 5.5
  - text: side
  - math "4.5 ≤ s is less than 5.5": 4.5 ≤ s < 5.5
  - text: perimeter
  - math "18 ≤ P is less than 22": 18 ≤ P < 22
  - text: Bounds in a calculation
  - img "Bounds in a calculation (Nova the cat, welcome)":
    - img "Nova the cat, goodbye"
  - img "Sir Bob Maximus, pleased"
  - text: Sir Bob Maximus · watch A square has side 5 centimetres to the nearest centimetre, so the side is from 4.5 up to 5.5. The perimeter is from 4 times 4.5 equals 18, up to 4 times 5.5 equals 22.
  - img "Nova the cat, cheering"
  - status: "Nova: Flawless. Like me."
  - group "Animation controls":
    - button "Reset"
    - button "Step back"
    - button "Play"
    - button "Step forward" [disabled]
    - text: Step 6 of 6 · Bounds in a calculation
    - slider "Scrub through steps": "5"
